subject: Private Offer: annualized term + overprovision safeguard
messages:
From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@medcore.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: MedCore Procurement <procurement@medcore.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Private Offer: annualized term + overprovision safeguard

Hi Hannah — thanks again for the demo last week. We ran this past our Cloud and Procurement teams and want to move forward with a private offer, but with two asks before we sign: 

1) Annualized term: we prefer a single 12-month annualized term starting Jan 1, 2027 (our fiscal cadence).
2) Overprovision safeguard: during our Q1 product launch we anticipate burst traffic. We need an agreed mechanism to allow a temporary overage (~20%) for up to 60 days without immediate termination or punitive uplift; we can accept a modest billing uplift for the overage but want a clear cap and automated roll-back.

I attached our PO template and SOC2 summary. Can Redwood propose the small contract addendum language and confirm whether the marketplace private offer flow can accommodate the burst clause (DocuSign + PO to follow).

Attachments: PrivateOffer_PO_Template_MedCore.docx (PO template), SOC2-summary-2026.pdf

Next steps we'd like: draft addendum, estimated cost delta for 20% burst (60 days), and a DocuSign link we can send to Procurement.

Thanks — Lisa
Lisa Chen
Head of Cloud Operations, MedCore Health
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@medcore.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, MedCore Procurement <procurement@medcore.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 10:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private Offer: annualized term + overprovision safeguard

Hi Lisa — really appreciate the clarity. We can support an annualized 12-month private offer and bake a short overage addendum into the private offer workflow. Two options to speed approval: 

- Option A (recommended): 12-month private offer + addendum that allows a capped temporary overage (20% for up to 60 days) billed at +15% uplift on incremental usage; automatic reversion to committed capacity after the window.
- Option B: Staggered tranches (90% commit / 10% burst pool) with a lower uplift but more procurement bookkeeping.

I'll draft the addendum and loop in our Marketplace lead for legal and billing sign-off. Karthik, can you confirm whether the marketplace private offer form will accept the addendum as a separate DocuSign envelope (preferred) or needs the clause embedded in the PO itself? I attached a quick note in the PO template where we'd put the addendum.

I'll put Marissa on the thread for final approval on the billing approach.

— Hannah Schmitt
Account Exec (Marketplace) | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@medcore.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private Offer: annualized term + overprovision safeguard

Thanks for the context — quick operational decision from my side to unblock: 

We will approve Option A with the following guardrails (legal + ops alignment):
- Addendum language: temporary overage allowance (20% for up to 60 days) billed on incremental usage at a +15% uplift; cap the total incremental charge as a percentage of committed annual spend (we typically set 30% cap for first-year launches).
- Auto-scaling control: overage triggers should be customer-initiated or Redwood-provisioned with notice; Redwood will notify billing contact at +24 hours and again at +72 hours.
- SLA tweak: no change to base latency SLA; surge capacity is best-effort beyond committed floor.

Karthik — legal redline recommended (3 minor edits to the addendum). I attached the commitment schedule spreadsheet showing where the overage sits versus committed tranches. Procurement — once legal signs the addendum we can generate a DocuSign envelope integrating the PO + addendum. Please share the billing contact and PO number.

Attachments: Redwood-Commitment-Schedule.xlsx

Lisa — following Marissa's approval, legal has prepared the addendum and I've packaged the PO + addendum into a DocuSign envelope. Summary below and link to sign: 

Summary of terms (high-level):
- 12-month term, Jan 1 2027–Dec 31 2027 (annualized).
- Committed capacity: per PO (see attached template).
- Overage window: up to 20% additional capacity for up to 60 days; incremental usage billed at +15% uplift; annual incremental charge capped at 30% of committed annual spend.
- Notifications: Redwood will notify billing contact at +24h and +72h during any overage window.

DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.com/embedded/abc123
Invoice & PO instructions: Invoice generated after DocuSign completion; Redwood can invoice monthly or in two tranches — let us know preference.

Attachments included with envelope: PrivateOffer_PO_Template_MedCore.docx, Redwood-Commitment-Schedule.xlsx, SOC2-summary-2026.pdf

Lisa — can you confirm billing contact and preferred invoice cadence so we include it in the envelope? Procurement — please route the envelope to the appropriate signer once Lisa confirms the PO number.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

— Hannah Schmitt
